surfaces.change: bale status classifies every open session on its own facts (_gather_open_session: its bale/<sid> branch, its outbox tarball, its clarification records, its stamped manifest), the lock session's facts filling the session_* fields as before; StatusReport gains search_dirs (the configured apply.search_paths list beside its count) and open_session_facts, each with the response tarballs the named search would find (status_response_files over the new numbered_copies). New newer_numbered_copy_note: when bale apply, bale retry or bale handoff is given a relative name that resolves and a numbered copy of it ('<name> (N).tar.gz') newer than the file sits in cwd or any search directory, the verb logs the copy's name, the word newer and the paste-ready line for it, and still uses the file it was named; an older copy, an absolute name or a missing copy changes nothing. Help texts: apply's resolution paragraph names the note and the clarification attempt, status --json names the new keys, contract names the HOLD classes, and the --cost-file help no longer says a clarification writes no attempt.

bale status --json gains the top-level open_sessions (appended after clipboard; one entry per open sid, keys exactly the sessions list, each {state, goal, expects_probe, clarification, responses}, null outside a repo), config.search_dirs (appended after summary_failed) and clipboard.encoding ('utf-16le' for clip.exe, 'utf-8' otherwise, null when nothing is copied; the new clipboard_encoding over clipboard_command_is_clip_exe); STATUS_REPORT_KEYS lists open_sessions last so every earlier key keeps its place. The human clipboard row for clip.exe ends ', fed to it as UTF-16LE'; another command's row is unchanged. bale contract publishes the vocabulary hold-class (home bin/bale_stats.py, pointer HOLD_CLASSES), read from bale_stats's own tuple through the new CONTRACT_SIBLING_CODE_HOMES; _contract_code_tuple takes the entry's home. A clarification's bale apply --json line names its telemetry record.

A clarification landing appends a clarification attempt to the session's telemetry record after preserving the round: outcome clarification, command the landing verb (apply, or retry), the clarification summary {rounds, records} as it then stands (rounds 1 on the first round), and the invocation's validated --cost-file block, which a clarification used to log as not stamped. The session stays open; its later normal response appends the attempt that closes it.

clarification joins IN_FLIGHT_OUTCOMES: a session whose latest attempt is a clarification landing is in flight, never a closure. Its command is apply or retry, so it counts in response_attempts beside a bailout's; it is never validated, so no agreement, hold or checkpoint rate moves. The dossier shows it among the attempts with its clarification rounds. HOLD_CLASSES' comment names bale contract as its publisher.
The envelope and attempt outcome enums gain clarification (additive, record_version stays 1); the outcome, command and clarification descriptions say what a clarification landing now writes.

5.5 names open_sessions, search_dirs and the clip.exe encoding; 5.9 names the hold-class vocabulary and its home; 8.1's tarball resolution names the newer-copy note; 8.9 and 8.10.2 say a clarification landing writes a clarification attempt (and carries --cost-file) instead of nothing; 8.11's relay paragraph keeps a recorded relay round writing no attempt.
The status, contract and clipboard notes name the new keys, the hold-class vocabulary's sibling home and the clarification attempt.
New suite pinning the eight outcomes, unit and end to end.
The clarification case now pins the attempt carrying the cost file, where it pinned the not-stamped log line.
The status --json clipboard object's key set includes encoding.
A code-homed vocabulary may name bin/bale_stats.py and is read from that module.
The 0.4.62 release pin checks its own changelog record and an install at or past 0.4.62, not bin/VERSION equal to it.

notes: Additive: no key is renamed, removed or re-meant. bale status --json's sid and session still describe the lock session (sessions[0], the first sid in sorted order); open_sessions describes every open session. A recorded bale relay round still writes no attempt. Records written before 0.4.63 carry no clarification attempt for their landings; a session whose latest attempt is a clarification reads in flight.
